note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Start the age readers once the ledger lands", the age rules reaching young writers, producers and directors as well as performers; "It should cover across every country"; "Again I want depth covering every basis for every feature leaving NO STONE UNTURNED"): what age changes for screen work in Serbia and Montenegro: the age of majority, the working age, how a minor's contract binds and what of the pay is set aside, a child performer's permit and hours, the unions', the funds' and the company law's ages. Research, retry and web-search subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-ages-roles.md, BRIEF-ages-world.md, BRIEF-ages-search.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: CS names the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, which ended when Montenegro declared independence on 3 June 2006; the Republic of Serbia continues its international personality (Constitutional Charter art. 60, National Assembly decision of 5 June 2006), so the age-of-majority rule is Serbia's (RS) for a life in Serbia and Montenegro's (ME) for a life in Montenegro; the code carries no law of its own.

value.law: Constitutional Charter of Serbia and Montenegro art. 60; Decision of the National Assembly of Serbia, 5 June 2006

figures.applies: Every place under CS reads RS or ME by where it lies; no State Union law is in force.
figures.webSearch: 2026-11-01: 'Constitutional Charter State Union Serbia and Montenegro article 60 Serbia successor continuity 2006 National Assembly decision 5 June 2006' returned the National Assembly of Serbia's 4 and 8 June 2006 pages (used), HCCH depositary notifications (used), ICCROM, Wikisource's Charter text, Wikipedia.

sources.said: membership of the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro in the Council of Europe, including all its bodies and instruments, was being continued by the Republic of Serbia under Article 60 of the Constitutional Charter of Serbia and Montenegro, the Declaration of Independence adopted by the Montenegrin parliament on 3 June 2006, and the Decision of the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia on Obligations of Public Authorities of the Republic of Serbia in Assuming Powers of the Republic of Serbia as Successor State to the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro of 5 June 2006.

Following the declaration of the state independence of Montenegro, and under the Article 60 of the Constitutional Charter of the state union of Serbia and Montenegro, the Republic of Serbia is continuing international personality of the state union of Serbia and Montenegro, which was confirmed also by the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia at its session held on 5 June 2006.
